title: Why Hailey Bieber Sold Her Beauty Brand

source.author: Amanda Gerut
source.title: Hailey Bieber sold Rhode to e.l.f. Beauty after she and cofounder Lauren Ratner addressed their main fear in an acquisition

paragraphs: Hailey Bieber is a celebrity, and she also started a business. In 2022, she launched Rhode, a beauty brand. Three years later, the company e.l.f. Beauty agreed to buy it in a deal worth up to $1 billion. On Wednesday, Bieber spoke about the acquisition at the Fortune Most Powerful Women Summit.

At the summit, Bieber said that selling her company was her one big fear. She worried that she would lose her say in the business. So before the deal, the founders wanted to retain control of Rhode's products and creative choices. According to Bieber, e.l.f. Beauty now lets them "continue to make every decision."

Why sell at all? Lauren Ratner, who started Rhode with Bieber, explained the reason. Rhode had a lean team, and the team had reached its limits. "We really needed the infrastructure of a bigger partner to scale globally," Ratner said. In other words, a lean company could not succeed in many countries alone. A larger partner can enable a small brand to grow much faster.

Sales are growing fast. Rhode had about $390 million in net sales in its fiscal year 2026, an 80% increase from the year before. The brand entered Sephora stores in the United States last September. According to Fortune, it then launched with Sephora in Europe, in 19 new markets and more than 500 stores. The size of its new owner helps enable this kind of growth overseas.

Ratner said Rhode is the number one brand in every retail market where it sells. In other words, she says it is the dominant brand. That is a strong claim, and the article does not give numbers for every market. Nevertheless, the popularity of the brand is clear from its sales. In Australia, for example, Rhode is the top brand at the beauty store Mecca.

Today, Bieber is the chief creative officer at Rhode, and Ratner is its president and chief brand officer. Both founders retain a big role, even after the sale. Nevertheless, as Bieber told the summit, the deal only worked for them because their main fear was answered first. If Rhode can keep its popularity and stay dominant in new markets, the founders will have reason to say the deal helped them succeed.
